findings.evidence: `DistribSMul.toLinearMap` requires only `[Semiring R] [Module R M] [Monoid S] [DistribSMul S M] [SMulCommClass S R M]` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/End.lean:241); the PR's hypotheses reach it via `IsScalarTower.to_smulCommClass'` (Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Basic.lean:427). Mathlib's own `e • N` construction uses the weak form: `Submodule.pointwiseDistribMulAction` under `[Monoid α] [DistribMulAction α M] [SMulCommClass α R M]` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/Pointwise.lean:183-190).
findings.fix: State the file over `[Semiring S] [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module S M] [Module R M] [SMulCommClass R S M]`. Downstream is unaffected: `ModuleDecomposition` keeps `Algebra k (pathAlgebra k Q)`/`IsScalarTower`, which supply `SMulCommClass` by instance. Fix the docstring claim (line 34) that the algebra+tower bundle is "exactly the data" of a central action — it is strictly stronger than `SMulCommClass`.
findings.issue: The scalar hypotheses `[CommSemiring S] [Algebra S R] [IsScalarTower S R M]` are stronger than needed and than Mathlib convention: `algebraMap` never appears in the file, and the bundle is used only to produce `SMulCommClass R S M` for `DistribSMul.toLinearMap S M e`. Same variable block at lines 125, 140, 182.

findings.evidence: Module.lean:144-147 and ModuleDecomposition.lean:118-127; `ofPath_mul_vertexIdempotent_of_ne` and `vertexIdempotent_mul_ofPath` in TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/PathAlgebra.lean are exactly the `r * e = 0` and `f * r = r` hypotheses.
findings.fix: Add the two primitive lemmas here — `(hr : r * e = 0) (he : IsIdempotentElem e) (hx : x ∈ smulRange S M e) : r • x = 0` and `(hr : f * r = r) : r • x ∈ smulRange S M f` (the latter needs no idempotency) — and derive `smul_eq_zero_of_mem_smulRange` (`r = e i`), `ofPath_smul_eq_zero_of_mem_vertexComponent` and `ofPath_smul_mem_vertexComponent` from them. The same generalisation gives `pathMap` as left multiplication `smulRange S M e →ₗ[S] smulRange S M f` by an `r` with `f * r * e = r`, with `pathMap_nil`/`pathMap_comp` (lines 148, 158) instances of its unit/multiplicativity.
findings.issue: `smul_eq_zero_of_mem_smulRange` is stated only for a member of an orthogonal family, so the same argument is re-run in the special case at ModuleDecomposition.lean:123 (`conv_lhs => rw [← vertexIdempotent_smul_of_mem_vertexComponent hx]; rw [smul_smul, ofPath_mul_vertexIdempotent_of_ne _ h, zero_smul]` versus `obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩; rw [smul_smul, he.ortho hij, zero_smul]`). The dual fact, ModuleDecomposition.lean:118 (`f * r = r` implies `r • x ∈ f • M`), has no general counterpart at all.

findings.evidence: `grep -rn smulRange_le_comap TauCeti` matches only its own declaration (Module.lean:130) and the docstring line 54; ModuleDecomposition.lean:177-179 discharges the same obligation with `rw [mem_vertexComponent_iff, ← map_smul f, ...]`.
findings.fix: Promote it to the map it exists for, `smulRangeMap (e : R) (f : M →ₗ[R] N) : smulRange S M e →ₗ[S] smulRange S N e := (f.restrictScalars S).restrict (smulRange_le_comap e f)`, and define `vertexComponentMap k f v := smulRangeMap _ f`.
findings.issue: `smulRange_le_comap` — the general "an `R`-linear map carries `e • M` into `e • N`" — has no use anywhere, while `vertexComponentMap` (ModuleDecomposition.lean:175) re-proves the same statement inline to build the restriction.

summary: The general file is stated over `Algebra S R` + `IsScalarTower S R M` where Mathlib's convention for exactly this construction is `SMulCommClass`, and it stops one lemma short of the facts the path-algebra file needs, so ModuleDecomposition re-proves three of them by hand while the general `smulRange_le_comap` sits unused.
